title: 1 vs 100
tagline: Microsoft pulled the plug in 2010. I plugged it back in.
insertQuote: I played a show myself with a controller
what: I play the original Xbox game show on my Linux PC, with a controller, a host voice of my own and a Mob of a hundred AI contestants. My show server runs the questions, lifelines, eliminations and money ladder.
built: Got the original Xbox 360 game running as a normal Linux program
A show server I wrote from scratch: the schedule, the questions, and a Mob of 100 AI players and their answers
All three helps, the show's lifelines, work: ask the Mob, ask a Crowd of 50, or ask the Top 10
A host voice of my own, fitted into the game's own lines, not a copy of the original host
Dressed avatars for the whole Mob, each with a fixed look and name
credit: Built it, on the ReXGlue recompiler and the 1 vs 100 Reborn team's fixes to it
starring: Me, and a hundred AI contestants
progress: I play as the One against the AI Mob.

making.problem: Microsoft shut the servers down in 2010. Without a show server, the original game had no show to join.
how: The game's original Xbox 360 program gets translated, function by function, into a normal Linux program.
Anything it expects from an Xbox (sign-in, the network, its own logging, avatars) is answered by code I wrote.
Instead of calling Microsoft, it calls a show server on my PC that runs the schedule, asks the questions and plays the Mob.
A control page starts the show: the game opens full screen and I play with a controller.

proof.caption: What the game says now when a show starts on my server. Then come the wall of a hundred AI contestants, the questions, the eliminations and the money ladder.

credits: Original game: Microsoft's 1 vs 100 for Xbox LIVE (2009 to 2010)
Kit fixes: the 1 vs 100 Reborn team
Revival, fixes, show server and host voice: me

moment.what: The evening it first worked, I played a show myself with a controller: the countdown, "YOU ARE THE ONE", a wall of a hundred AI contestants, and a host who isn't the original guy.
